newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy approves emergency measures for milk sector. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Italy approves emergency measures for milk sector. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]

text.p: The Italian government on Thursday approved a package of emergency measures including cheap loans for the dairy sector to help farmers hit by harsh European Union fines for milk overproduction, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said.
"We have decided to respect the law but to give as much help as possible to help farmers in difficulty," Prodi told a news conference after a cabinet meeting.
The package of measures, contained in a decree law, is part of a wider drive to overhaul Italy's dairy sector.
The government said in a statement later that farmers would be granted soft five-year loans of up to 350 billion ($220 million) at 2.8 (corrects from 22.8) percent interest.
In order to help cover such loans, the government will set aside 150 billion lire ($100 million) for 1997-99.

Farmers have taken to the roads on tractors in two weeks of protests to press demands for the government to pay the EU milk fines, which are due by Friday and add up to some 370 billion lire ($230 million).
Prodi has sought a deal with the farmers for them to pay a first 25 percent instalment of the levies pending a full inquiry by a special commission that will be set up.
The commission will be charged with examining the application of the quotas and any potential sales infringements.
Prodi told the news conference that a full inventory of the national herds would also be carried out.
The government has said it is waiting to hear whether the EU will accept its proposals and Prodi promised to illustrate "the anomalous Italian situation" in Brussels personally.
The dispute centres on EU fines for overshooting Italy's 1995-96 milk quota by some 400,000 tonnes. Farmers say the government carries the responsibility for the overproduction.

Under the quota system, farmers are allowed to produce 9.9 million tonnes of milk, compared with Italy's total consumption of 18 million tonnes. Agriculture Minister Michele Pinto has asked the EU to raise Italy's quota to 10.5 million tonnes.
"No other European country imports six million tonnes of milk," Prodi told the news conference. "If this were petrol, it would be a very big pipeline."
The government statement said that Italy had won an undertaking from the EU that reform of the EU milk quota system, due to have been carried out in 1999, would begin in March.

Prodi appealed to farmers, some of whom continued their road blocks on Thursday amid tense stand-offs with police, to end their demonstrations peacefully and said he had done as much to help them as possible under EU laws.
But in Treviso in northern Italy, one farmers group said it was ready to march to Belgium to draw attention to its plight.
